hero.lede: MusicButler is a music bot you run yourself. Real YouTube and YouTube Music playback through slash commands — no API keys to buy, no third-party server sitting on your queue.
features.title: Built for reliability, not a demo
features.lede: Most Discord music bots run on someone else's server and break the moment YouTube changes something. This one runs in your own container, and it handles authentication the right way.
feature.architecture.title: Architecture
feature.architecture.desc: One Node.js process — no gRPC workers, no extra transport layer just trying to keep two services in sync.
feature.speed.title: Speed
feature.speed.desc: Audio passes straight through as raw Opus, no re-encoding. It also prebuffers ahead of the stream so playback doesn't stutter at the start.
feature.stability.title: Stability
feature.stability.desc: If a stream drops it reconnects on its own with backoff, and every connection has an error listener so a failure ends up in your logs instead of just going quiet.
feature.lightweight.title: Lightweight
feature.lightweight.desc: Voice encryption is pure JS, so there's nothing to compile. Runs fine even when there's barely any memory to spare.
feature.privacy.title: Privacy
feature.privacy.desc: It's all running on your own machine. The only network calls it makes are to Discord and YouTube — nobody else sees your cookies or your queue.
feature.easy.title: Easy to host
feature.easy.desc_html: Clone it, drop in an .env, and docker compose up. That's really the whole setup.
deploy.title: Set it up in four steps
deploy.lede: MusicButler ships as a Docker image, so there's nothing to install by hand beyond Docker itself.
deploy.step2_html: Grab your YouTube cookies and Discord bot token, and put them in a .env file.
deploy.step3_html: Drop that .env next to docker-compose.yml in the project root.
deploy.step4_html: Run it, invite the bot, and start playing.
